Ray Charles - Hit the Road Jack (1961)

This was written by Ray's good friend Percy Mayfield, an R&B singer who was badly disfigured in a car accident soon after he started performing. Mayfield cut back his touring and made his mark as a prolific songwriter, with many of his compositions performed by Charles. It was first recorded in 1960 as an a cappella demo sent to Art Rupe. It became famous after it was recorded by Ray Charles with The Raelettes vocalist Margie Hendrix. They were lovers for a time, but the song is not about their relationship.

"Hit the Road Jack" won a Grammy award for Best Rhythm and Blues Recording, placed in the Grammy Hall of Fame, and is ranked number 387 on Rolling Stone magazine's list of "The 500 Greatest Songs of All Time".
